case.case_title: Nalika Kumudini, Attorney-at-Law, (on behalf of Malsha Kumari) v. Nihal Mahinda, O.I.C. Hungama Police and Others
case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, S.C. Application (F.R.) No. 615/95, decided on 28 August 1997

clause.text: No person shall be arrested except according to law and must be informed of the reason.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the arrest of the petitioner, a 14-year-old girl, was lawful and in accordance with Article 13(1) of the Constitution, including whether she was informed of the reason for her arrest.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed she was unlawfully arrested at her house without proper legal procedure and was not informed of the reason for her arrest. She was also subjected to assault and torture by police officers.
case_context.respondent_argument: The 1st respondent denied the petitioner was at the police station or arrested by police on that day, and claimed the injuries were caused by the petitioner’s father. The police version denied unlawful arrest and detention.
key_facts: Petitioner was arrested at her house by police without proper procedure.
She was assaulted and tortured by police officers including the 1st respondent.
She was detained without being produced before a Magistrate.
Petitioner was not informed properly of the reason for her arrest.
Medical evidence showed injuries consistent with unlawful detention and assault.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The Court held that Article 13(1) requires that no person be arrested except according to law and that the person must be informed of the reason for the arrest. The petitioner’s arrest was unlawful as it did not comply with these requirements.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The Court found the petitioner was arrested unlawfully without being informed of the reason and was detained without legal authority. The injuries and circumstances corroborated the unlawful arrest and detention.
principles_established: Arrest must be lawful and according to legal procedure.
The arrested person must be informed of the reason for arrest.
Unlawful arrest infringes fundamental rights under Article 13(1).
precedents_cited: Premadasa v. Officer-in-Charge of the Hakmana Police, S.C. 127/94

outcome.holding: The Court held that the petitioner’s arrest was unlawful and infringed Article 13(1) of the Constitution.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: The Court awarded compensation to the petitioner and ordered protection against harassment.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(1) was central to the Court’s determination that the petitioner’s arrest was unlawful and that her fundamental rights were infringed, leading to the grant of relief.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The Court found the arrest and detention of the girl without producing her before a Magistrate were unlawful and that she was subjected to torture, infringing her rights under Articles 11, 13(1) and 13(2).
